name: CANDLES
full_name: CAlcium fluoride for studies of Neutrino and Dark matters by Low Energy Spectrometer
summary: CANDLES studies calcium-48 double-beta decay in calcium-fluoride scintillators at Kamioka. The isotope has a high decay energy, helping separate a possible signal from much of the natural gamma background.
detection_principle: Pure CaF2 crystals act as source and scintillator. Surrounding liquid scintillator provides an active veto, while pulse shapes and event timing reject internal radioactive sequences.

status.label: Operating / data taking
status.evidence: The CANDLES-III analysis reported a low-background search and a half-life constraint, rather than an observed neutrinoless decay.

collaboration.name: CANDLES Collaboration
lead_institutions: Osaka University Research Center for Nuclear Physics

results.summary: The CANDLES-III analysis reported a low-background search and a half-life constraint, rather than an observed neutrinoless decay.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
